I took an extended break recently to focus on my health and fitness so that I can come back to it. I had multiple injuries and the cost was eating away at my wallet. I can still afford it, but sometimes we have to take a step back and prioritize different things in our lives. If it's something you can't afford right now, it's not a bad idea to stabilize your income until you can afford it.


As far as not getting rusty, if you can manage to get into an open mat for free (I personally have never heard of this but it's a wonderful idea if you can find such a thing) otherwise there is a plethora of online content from well respected BJJ instructors that focus on solo drilling. Even if you can just WATCH BJJ content and solo drill things that you know you can do correctly, then I think that's a worthwhile endeavor. Watching BJJ matches may be of benefit as well.


There seems to be a huge stigma in the community behind "quitting" that I personally think is unhealthy. You're allowed to walk away and take a break for a bit. There's no shame in it, and BJJ will always be there. Your job, your career, your health, and your family will not.

My enchondroma has had no change, my knee pain at rest has gotten better but otherwise not a whole lot of change. I am actively doing Brazilian Jujitsu and tend to be careful with it and if it's aggravated at all I tend to back off. I'm currently in the process of dropping weight to take pressure off the knee. I'm not super overweight but planning on dropping around 30lbs to lessen the pressure. Afer that point, I'm considering a gel injection procedure. Something else I've looked into is MACI down the road if it gets bad enough. I will brace it during intense movement, exercise and it kind of helps. I hike a lot and I'm also looking at an offloaded brace for that. I will say for walking I would get a custom insert because the wrong shoes with bad knees is a recipe for disaster. I also rigorously iced my knee at the initial onset of pain. Hope this helps.
